objective: Prevent a nearly full Windows system volume from making the LabelAgent workbench appear frozen or corrupt an in-progress save, while keeping the formal state, model services, candidates, truth, training approval, and OSS unchanged.

diagnosis.finding: TEMP and TMP were already redirected to D:, so checking the inherited temporary directory alone concealed the critically low C: system volume. The final implementation checks the Windows system volume, inherited temp volume, and selected runtime-temp volume independently.

behavior: Print an explicit startup advisory when the Windows system volume has less than 2 GiB free.
Place all workbench temporary files in the LabelAgent D: runtime-temp directory even when inherited TEMP already points elsewhere.
Refuse a new workbench or isolated-workbench start when its selected runtime-temp volume has less than 256 MiB free, rather than risking partial writes.
Apply the same bounded runtime-temp preparation to isolated acceptance workbenches.

intermediate_candidate.problem: The first deployed draft checked the inherited TEMP path, which was D:/AI/Temp, and therefore did not warn about C:.
intermediate_candidate.resolution: The final candidate derives and checks the Windows system drive separately, then was retested and redeployed.

live_acceptance.startup_warning_observed: Windows system volume C:\ had 0.17 GiB free; workbench temp fixed to D:\Apps\LabelAgent\.local\runtime-temp\workbench-8765 with 23.60 GiB free.

cleanup.scope: Only reconstructible __pycache__ and .pytest_cache directories inside this exact worktree, plus the empty D: test-temp directory.
cleanup.finding: The small cache total proves the wider C: shortage was not caused mainly by this LabelAgent test run; unrelated C: content was left untouched.

boundary: This protects LabelAgent runtime temporary writes and exposes the low-system-volume condition at startup. It does not free the broader C: volume, guarantee Windows-wide stability at 0.17 GiB free, improve segmentation accuracy, prove cross-dataset generalization, or constitute SAM fine-tuning.
